summary: Dedicated static ServiceAccount manifests plus default-disabled service-account token automount wiring for messenger, mail, social, and community FD-001 dogfood tenant workload charts and rendered snapshots.
claim_boundary: This slice adds source-controlled Kubernetes ServiceAccount templates/snapshots and Pod-level automountServiceAccountToken=false defaults for FD-001 backbone dogfood workload charts. It proves static chart/snapshot identity hardening and CI-smoke regression coverage only; it does not claim Kubernetes API admission, live ServiceAccount creation, RBAC permissions, TokenReview, projected or bound token issuance, cloud workload identity federation, namespace creation, ArgoCD sync/health, branch-protection state, remote CI green, or production tenant workload deployment. FD-001 product delivery remains the master-plan product goal; Oyatie Cloud is the future dogfood substrate/proof point.

best_practice_research.used_for: Grounds explicit ServiceAccount assignment, least-privilege RBAC posture, and setting Pod automountServiceAccountToken=false when application Pods do not need Kubernetes API credentials.
Grounds tenant workload isolation as a composition of namespace-scoped identities, RBAC, network policy, quotas, and data-plane hardening without claiming a live cluster.
Confirms the existing restricted-style Pod posture stays in place while this slice only changes identity/token mount defaults.
Records that network isolation remains a separate required live/static follow-up for strict multi-tenant posture; this slice does not claim NetworkPolicy coverage for the k8s Helm charts.

repo_local_context.use: Existing FD-001 dogfood Deployments already had serviceAccountName, runtimeClassName, restricted-style securityContext, topology spread, probes, resources, tenant/cost labels, and Cosign annotations, but they relied on Kubernetes default token automount behavior.
Existing chart values had ServiceAccount names but no explicit automountToken policy or non-claim text.
Existing backbone CI smoke already parses FD-001 dogfood values/templates/snapshots and now blocks ServiceAccount/token-automount regressions.

findings: Small chart/snapshot hardening with no new controller, runtime dependency, API schema, or service code path.
Uses a single values switch per service for token automount so future live controllers can override intentionally instead of inheriting Kubernetes defaults implicitly.
Dedicated ServiceAccount identity and default-disabled token automount reduce unnecessary API credentials in future FD-001 tenant workloads.
The claim remains static/source-controlled; no live Oyatie Cloud identity federation, TokenReview, or RBAC enforcement is asserted.

A RED static check failed before implementation for every service: missing serviceAccount.automountToken=false, missing Deployment automountServiceAccountToken, missing ServiceAccount template, missing rendered Deployment automount=false, and missing rendered ServiceAccount snapshot.
Governance smoke now semantically parses the expanded snapshot set and fails if rendered ServiceAccounts or rendered Deployments lose false automount posture.
Operators can find the identity hardening knob under the existing serviceAccount values block; the default is safe for first-party app Pods that do not call the Kubernetes API.
Source templates and rendered snapshots remain parseable YAML/Helm text and preserve existing tenant/cost labels, topology spread, resources, probes, and security contexts.
CI smoke parses 51 files after adding ServiceAccount templates and rendered snapshots.
Rejected relying on Kubernetes default ServiceAccount behavior because Kubernetes automatically mounts assigned ServiceAccount credentials unless disabled at Pod or ServiceAccount level.

Rejected adding RBAC bindings in this slice because these application Pods do not yet prove a need to call the Kubernetes API; zero RBAC grants is safer and keeps live identity federation as an explicit future slice.
Rejected broad NetworkPolicy changes here to keep this slice identity-focused; network isolation remains an explicitly recorded follow-up/non-claim.
No secrets, credentials, tokens, RBAC permissions, cloud identities, or tenant data are added.
The static rendered Pod specs now explicitly disable automatic ServiceAccount token projection.
Existing restricted-style pod/container security posture is left intact.
No Rust runtime, SQL, broker, gRPC, REST, or hot-path code changes. Kubernetes metadata only.
ServiceAccount templates and snapshots carry the existing tenant, cost-center, workload-class, regulatory-pack, dogfood-substrate, and product-goal labels for future audit/cost/policy correlation.
Explicit non-claim annotations prevent static manifests from being misread as live cluster/RBAC evidence.
Rollback removes the ServiceAccount templates/snapshots, automount lines, values keys, and CI smoke checks without data migration or public API impact.
Workload identity labels provide future observability/cost/audit joins, but no live telemetry is emitted by this static slice.
No Deployment selector labels or service endpoints change.

If a later workload legitimately needs Kubernetes API access, the safe follow-up path is an explicit serviceAccount.automountToken override plus least-privilege RBAC in a reviewed live or tenant-specific slice.
Uses existing CS-BACKBONE slice naming and existing oya-<service> ServiceAccount names from chart values.
Updates task plan/todo and multispectrum evidence only; no new root Markdown or retired external coordination surface.
Identity hardening lives in per-service Kubernetes Helm chart directories and static rendered dogfood snapshots.
Infrastructure chart contract only; no domain/usecase/adapter boundary drift.
No Cargo, npm, Helm, container, or provider dependency changes.
No data schema or algorithm changes. The new values fields are serviceAccount.automountToken and serviceAccount.nonClaim.
Backbone governance smoke now blocks missing ServiceAccount templates/snapshots and missing false automount defaults for all four FD-001 dogfood workloads.
